Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan (July/August 644 or June/July 647 - 9 October 705), was the fifth Umayyad caliph, ruling from April 685 until his death in October 705.
Nicknamed the 'Knight King' or 'Soldier King' for his role in World War I, this Belgian monarch succeeded his uncle Leopold II to the throne in 1909 — who was he?
Albert I of Belgium (8 April 1875 - 17 February 1934) was King of the Belgians from 23 December 1909 until his death in 1934.
Born in the colonial Carolinas and married to Rachel Donelson, this Army general turned seventh U.S. president lent his name to a whole democratic movement — who is he?
Andrew Jackson (March 15, 1767 - June 8, 1845) was the seventh president of the United States from 1829 to 1837.
Married to Benazir Bhutto in 1987, this politician later served two separate terms as Pakistan's president, decades apart — who is he?
Asif Ali Zardari (born 26 July 1955) is a Pakistani politician who has served as the 14th president of Pakistan since 2024.
George Washington trusted this major general enough to hand him command of West Point — which he then schemed to surrender to the British in 1780. Who was the would-be turncoat?
Benedict Arnold was British military officer (1741–1801).

A former Unilever executive who rose to CEO of Air New Zealand, he became leader of the Opposition in 2021 and prime minister two years later — who is he?
Christopher Luxon (born 19 July 1970) is a New Zealand politician and businessman who has served as the 42nd prime minister of New Zealand since 2023.
Nicknamed the 'King of the Wild Frontier,' this American frontiersman represented Tennessee in the U.S. House of Representatives before dying while fighting in the Texas Revolution — who is he?
Davy Crockett (August 17, 1786 - March 6, 1836) was an American politician, militia officer and frontiersman.
Followers of this modern movement pick careers and donate to charities based on rigorous cost-benefit calculations, aiming to maximize positive impact worldwide — what movement is this?
Effective altruism (EA) is a 21st-century philosophical and social movement that advocates impartially calculating benefits and prioritizing causes to provide the greatest good.
This former guerrilla movement, born from a 1980 merger of leftist Salvadoran factions, later became a political party after El Salvador's long civil war ended in 1992 — which group?
Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front is a Salvadoran left-wing political party and former guerrilla rebel group.
Speaking a Continental Celtic language and bearing the hallmarks of La Tène culture, this Iron Age people spread across what is now France, Belgium, and beyond — who were they?
Gauls (Ancient) were a group of Celtic peoples of mainland Europe in the Iron Age and the Roman period (roughly 5th century BC to 5th century AD).

Schooled in exile in the US and Argentina after his party's founder was ousted, he came home to lead the opposition coalition against a military dictatorship — and served as Panama's president from 1989 to 1994. Who was he?
Guillermo Endara (May 12, 1936 - September 28, 2009) was a Panamanian politician who served as the president of Panama from 1989 to 1994.
Cast off Mount Olympus by his mother due to a congenital impairment, this Greek god presided over fire, metalworking, and volcanoes — who is he?
Hephaestus (eight spellings; Ancient) is the Greek god of artisans, blacksmiths, carpenters, craftsmen, fire, metallurgy, metalworking, sculpture, and volcanoes.
Known to the Romans as Somnus, this Greek god of sleep is the namesake behind a word for an induced trance — who is he?
Hypnos (Ancient), also spelled Hypnus, is the personification of sleep.
This criminal-defence lawyer represented Bramalea—Gore—Malton in Ontario's legislature before leading a major Canadian federal party from 2017 to 2025 — who is he?

Jagmeet Singh (born January 2, 1979) is a Canadian politician and lawyer who served as the leader of the New Democratic Party (NDP) from 2017 to 2025 and as the member of Parliament (MP) for Burnaby South from 2019 to 2025.

Having left school at 13 to join Melbourne's labour movement, this Labor leader served as Australia's prime minister through most of WWII's Pacific war and is often ranked among the nation's greatest — who was he?
John Curtin (8 January 1885 - 5 July 1945) was an Australian politician who served as the 14th prime minister of Australia from 1941 until his death in 1945.
This politician represents the Sircilla constituency in the Telangana Legislative Assembly and was named Most Inspirational Icon of 2015 by a major Indian broadcaster — who is he?
K. T. Rama Rao (born 24 July 1976), commonly known as KTR, is an Indian politician and Member of Legislative Assembly (MLA) of Telangana Legislative Assembly.
This American politician served as South Dakota's governor before becoming the eighth U.S. secretary of homeland security in 2025 — who is she?
Kristi Noem (NOHM; ne Arnold; born November 30, 1971) is an American politician serving as the United States special envoy for the Shield of the Americas since 2026.
Before becoming the 28th U.S. secretary of defense, this retired Army general was the first African American to command U.S. Central Command — who is he?
Lloyd Austin (born August 8, 1953) is a retired United States Army general who served as the 28th United States secretary of defense, from 2021 to 2025, under the Biden administration.
Born into the House of Valois in Lorraine, this queen consort of Henry VI became a driving force of the Lancastrian cause in the Wars of the Roses — who is she?
Margaret of Anjou (23 March 1430 - 25 August 1482) was Queen of England by marriage to King Henry VI from 1445 to 1461 and again from 1470 to 1471.
A poet and broadcaster who entered politics through the Labour Party, this Irishman served as mayor of Galway before becoming president of Ireland from 2011 to 2025 — who is he?
Michael D. Higgins (born 18 April 1941) is an Irish politician, poet and broadcaster who served as the president of Ireland from November 2011 to November 2025.

This Indian lawyer and Indian National Congress leader served as party president from 1919 to 1920 and again from 1928 to 1929, and fathered the man who would become independent India's first prime minister — who is he?
Motilal Nehru (6 May 1861 - 6 February 1931) was an Indian lawyer, activist, and politician affiliated with the Indian National Congress.
Before becoming France's president in 2007, this Paris-born politician served as mayor of Neuilly-sur-Seine and led the UMP party — who is it?
Nicolas Sarkozy (sar-KOH-zee; born 28 January 1955) is a French former politician who served as the president of France from 2007 to 2012.

This American showman built fame on celebrated hoaxes and co-founded a legendary circus — though he insisted the cynical phrase 'there's a sucker born every minute' was wrongly pinned on him — who was he?
P. T. Barnum (July 5, 1810 - April 7, 1891) was an American showman, businessman, and politician remembered for promoting celebrated hoaxes and founding the Ringling Bros.
The fifth Roman governor of Judaea under Tiberius, he's named in both the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds — and is even venerated as a saint by the Ethiopian Orthodox Church. Who is he?
Pontius Pilate was the fifth governor of the Roman province of Judaea, serving under Emperor Tiberius from 26/27 to 36/37 AD.
Nicknamed 'electric brain' for his calm under pressure, this U.S. admiral commanded Task Force 16 at Midway, where American dive bombers sank four Japanese fleet carriers — who was he?
Raymond A. Spruance (July 3, 1886 - December 13, 1969) was a United States Navy admiral during World War II.

Sparked in 1917 amid wartime bread shortages and battlefield defeats, this upheaval abolished a monarchy and installed a socialist government after two successive uprisings and a civil war — what is it called?
Russian Revolution was a period of political and social change in Russia, starting in 1917.
This liberal, pro-European Ukrainian party takes its name from a sitcom starring the man who'd go on to become the country's real president — which party?
Servant of the People (SN) is a liberal, centrist, pro-European political party in Ukraine.
This ruler quelled a rebellion in Gdańsk and worked closely with chancellor Jan Zamoyski during his decade as king of Poland — who was he?

This German politician has co-chaired the far-right Alternative for Germany party since 2019 alongside Alice Weidel, and is known for pro-Russian, eurosceptic foreign-policy views. Who is he?
Tino Chrupalla (born 14 April 1975) is a German politician from the far-right party Alternative for Germany (AfD).
After heading the Soviet gas ministry, this man became Gazprom's first chairman, then Russia's Prime Minister for six years during the transition from a planned to a market economy — who is he?
Viktor Chernomyrdin (9 April 1938 - 3 November 2010) was a Soviet and Russian politician and businessman.
Praised for strategy but condemned for scorched-earth tactics against the Confederacy, this Ohio-born Union general from a politically prominent family graduated West Point in 1840 — who was he?
William Tecumseh Sherman (tih-; February 8, 1820 - February 14, 1891) was an American businessman, author, and United States Army general in the Union Army during the American Civil War (1861-1865).

After 30 years without one, France got a woman back in its top government post in May 2022—the second ever to hold it. A civil engineer and transport minister, who took the reins during a time of national transition?

Élisabeth Borne (born 18 April 1961) is a French politician who served as Prime Minister of France from May 2022 to January 2024, becoming the second woman to hold the position of Prime Minister and the first in 30 years.
A glider pilot who flew 705 combat missions and survived being shot down four times, this Luftwaffe ace racked up 104 aerial victories, all against the Western Allies — who is he?
Adolf Galland: German World War II flying ace and general.

Alboin: King of the Lombards from c. 560 to 572.

Amenhotep II: Seventh Pharaoh of the Eighteenth dynasty of Egypt. Amenhotep II (lit. '"Amun is Satisfied"'), also called Amenophis II, was the seventh pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt.
Henry VIII's marriage to his fourth wife lasted barely six months in 1540, doomed partly because a portrait by Hans Holbein flattered her more than reality did — who was she?
Anne of Cleves: Queen of England in 1540.

In December 1984 more than 500,000 people near a pesticide plant in Madhya Pradesh were exposed to which highly toxic gas?

Renowned as the fabulously wealthy last king of Lydia, he was ultimately defeated by Cyrus the Great after the siege of Sardis — who was he?
Croesus: King of Lydia from 585 or 561 to 547 BC.

Formed in 1988 as a liberal youth movement opposing Hungary's Marxist-Leninist government, this party transformed into a right-wing force that dominated Hungarian politics under Viktor Orbán — which party?
Fidesz: Political party in Hungary. It was the country's main ruling party from 1998 to 2002 and dominated Hungarian politics from 2010 to 2026 during the Orbán era.

Split by historians into 'first' and 'second' phases — the second launched by an 1830 conquest of Algiers — this overseas empire was, before World War I, the world's second-largest after Britain's — whose empire?
French colonial empire: Overseas territories controlled by France (1534–1980)

Hera: Goddess from Greek mythology, wife and sister of Zeus.
Officially known as Ansar Allah, this Zaydi Shia movement emerged in Yemen in the 1990s and is now backed by Iran as part of the 'Axis of Resistance.' Which group is this?
Houthis: Shia Islamist organization in Yemen.

Founded in 1885 as the first modern nationalist movement anywhere in the British Empire's Asian or African territories, this century-old big-tent party was later led by Mahatma Gandhi toward independence — which party?
Indian National Congress: Political party in India.

Judaism: Religion of the Jewish people.
Pulled from the Apollo 13 crew three days before launch, this astronaut then helped guide the crippled ship home before flying to the Moon himself on Apollo 16 — who is it?
Born in Japan to a Chinese father, this Southern Ming general expelled the Dutch from Taiwan and founded the Kingdom of Tungning — by what honorific title is he known?
Koxinga: Founder of the Tungning Kingdom of Taiwan.
This king surrendered his country to German invaders in 1940, sparking postwar controversy that nearly caused a civil war upon his return home in 1950 — who was he?
Leopold III of Belgium: King of the Belgians from 1934 to 1951.
Crowned King of France at just five years old after his great-grandfather's death, he reigned nearly 59 years — the second-longest in French history — and was nicknamed "the Beloved." Who was he?
Louis XV: King of France from 1715 to 1774.
King of Alba from 1058 to 1093, this ruler was later nicknamed "Canmore," understood to mean "great chief." His 35-year reign preceded the Scoto-Norman age—who was he?
Malcolm III of Scotland: King of Alba from 1058 to 1093. Throughout his reign, Malcolm III led at least five invasions into English territory.

A member of the Cherokee Nation who once ran his family's plumbing business, this politician moved from Oklahoma's House delegation to the Senate before becoming U.S. secretary of homeland security in 2026 — who is he?
Markwayne Mullin: American politician and businessman (born 1977)
Spanning 1868 to 1912, this period saw Japan transform from an isolated feudal society into a modern industrial power under Western influence. What era, named for the reigning emperor, was it?
Meiji era: Period of Japanese history (1868–1912)
A former member of an elite Croatian police tactical unit, this fighter's ring nickname referenced that job, and he won the 2006 Pride Open-Weight Grand Prix?

Launched in 2017 by Crown Prince Mohammad bin Salman, this Saudi megaproject at the northern tip of the Red Sea was eventually scaled way back amid delays, cost overruns, and criticism — what is it?

Renowned for his cunning intelligence, this legendary king of Ithaca spent ten eventful years just trying to get home after the Trojan War — who is he?
Odysseus: Legendary Greek king of Ithaca. Odysseus also plays a key role in Homer's Iliad and other works in that same epic cycle.

Known to the Rus as the Obri and to the Göktürks as the Apar, this nomadic confederation ruled a khaganate centered on the Carpathian Basin from the late sixth to early ninth centuries — who were they?
Pannonian Avars: Alliance of various Eurasian nomads – 6th to 9th centuries.

Born in what is now Syria, this Roman emperor reigned from 244 to 249 during an unusually stable stretch of a turbulent century, after being proclaimed ruler when his predecessor died in battle — who is he?
Philip the Arab: Roman emperor from 244 to 249. Philip I (Latin: Marcus Julius Philippus; c. 204 – September 249), commonly known as Philip the Arab, was Roman emperor from 244 to 249.
A member of India's storied Nehru dynasty, this Indian National Congress politician has represented Wayanad in Kerala in the Lok Sabha since November 2024 — who is she?

Rooted in a Greek word meaning 'to snatch away' from First Thessalonians, this end-times evangelical belief holds that living and dead Christians alike will rise to meet Christ in the clouds — what is it called?

An Iraqi politician who served as the fifth president from 1979 until his overthrow in 2003 during the US-led invasion, previously a vice president and prime minister—who was he?
Saddam Hussein: President of Iraq from 1979 to 2003. The policies and ideologies he championed are collectively known as Saddamism, a right-wing variant of Ba'athism.
Scientology grew out of a system L. Ron Hubbard first presented in 1950 as a form of talk therapy. What was it called?
Hubbard published Dianetics in 1950 as therapy, then reframed it as a religion and founded the Church of Scientology in 1953.
After a stint as a teacher, this man rose to become the first democratically elected president of Nigeria when the military handed over power in 1979, launching the Second Republic — who was he?
Shehu Shagari: President of Nigeria from 1979 to 1983.
An architect by training who once served as mayor of Quito, this man won Ecuador's presidency on his third try in 1992 after founding a new conservative party — who is it?
Sixto Durán Ballén: President of Ecuador from 1992 to 1996.
Established by Seljuk Turks after their victory over Byzantine forces at Manzikert in 1071, this Turco-Persian state is considered the beginning of Turkish history in Anatolia. What was it?
Sultanate of Rum: Turkish state in central Anatolia from 1077 to 1308.
This biblical figure, son of Nahor, is best known as the father of the patriarch Abraham in the Book of Genesis — who is he?
Terah: Figure in the Hebrew Bible; son of Nahor.

The third shōgun of a ruling dynasty, this Japanese leader closed the country's borders to Europeans and persecuted Christians during his 1623-1651 reign, a policy that lasted over two centuries — who is he?
Tokugawa Iemitsu: Japanese Samurai, Daimyo and Military leader of Japan from 1623 to 1651.
A trained physician who served as Germany's Defence Minister under Angela Merkel, she has led the European Commission since 2019 — who is she?
Ursula von der Leyen: President of the European Commission since 2019. Von der Leyen was born and raised in Brussels, Belgium, to German parents.
Canonized as a saint by both the Catholic and Orthodox churches, this Rurik dynasty ruler seized Kiev with a Varangian army in 978 after his brothers' deadly feud — who is he?
Vladimir the Great: Grand Prince of Kiev from 978 to 1015.

After nine years as a CIA clandestine officer, this politician represented a sprawling 550-mile Texas border district in Congress before mounting a brief 2024 presidential bid and endorsing Nikki Haley — who is he?
Born in the Khan Yunis refugee camp and educated at the Islamic University of Gaza, he rose to lead Hamas in Gaza before being killed in a 2024 clash with the IDF — who was he?
Yahya Sinwar: Palestinian militant and politician (1962–2024)
Before becoming Colombia's 32nd president in 2002, this leader of the right-wing Democratic Center party served as mayor of Medellín, then governor of Antioquia — who is he?
Álvaro Uribe: President of Colombia from 2002 to 2010.

Nobelium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol No and atomic number 102.
In what year was Alexander Hamilton born?
Alexander Hamilton: Born out of wedlock in Charlestown on the Caribbean island of Nevis, Hamilton was orphaned as a child and taken in by a prosperous merchant.
In what year did Albert Einstein die?
Albert Einstein (14 March 1879 – 18 April 1955) was a German-born theoretical physicist best known for developing the known theory of relativity.
In what year was Calcium discovered?
Calcium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ca and atomic number 20.
Which company manufactures Boeing F/A-18E/F Super Hornet?
Boeing F/A-18E/F Super Hornet: McDonnell Douglas. The Super Hornet is in service with the armed forces of the United States, Australia, and Kuwait.
Which country is Artemy Lebedev from?
Artemy Lebedev: Russia. Artemy Andreyevich Lebedev (Russian: Артемий Андреевич Лебедев; born 13 February 1975) is a Russian designer, entrepreneur and Internet personality.
Who is credited with discovering Cadmium?
Cadmium: Friedrich Stromeyer. Cadmium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cd and atomic number 48.
Who is credited with discovering Pigeonhole principle?

Pigeonhole principle: Johann Peter Gustav Lejeune Dirichlet. In mathematics, the pigeonhole principle states that if n items are put into m containers, with n > m, then at least one container must contain more than one item.
Who is credited with discovering Galactic Center?
Galactic Center: Harlow Shapley. The Galactic Center is the barycenter of the Milky Way and a corresponding point on the rotational axis of the galaxy.
First unearthed in Montana in 1987 by a team led by Jack Horner, this horned dinosaur genus takes its name from a Greek river deity — name the genus?
Achelousaurus is a genus of centrosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous Period of what is now North America, about 77 to 74.8 million years ago.

This South African bulb genus tends to flower around March, earning a local nickname tied to that month, and is often confused with the Hippeastrum plants sold at Christmas under its common name — which genus?
Amaryllis is the only genus in the subtribe Amaryllidinae (tribe Amaryllideae).
Known as 'doodlebugs' for the trails they leave in sand, these insect larvae dig pits to ambush wandering ants, while the winged adults are often mistaken for dragonflies — what are they?
Antlion are a group of about 2,000 species of insect in the neuropteran family Myrmeleontidae.
Despite the name, this gold-brown-eyed black-and-white bird of Australia isn't related to its Eurasian namesake at all — it's a butcherbird cousin in its own genus. What is it?
Australian magpie (Gymnorhina tibicen) is a black and white passerine bird native to Australia and southern New Guinea, and introduced to New Zealand, and the Fijian island of Taveuni.
What yellow-green digestive fluid is produced continuously by the liver but stored and concentrated in the gallbladder until it's needed to break down fats in the small intestine?
Bile (from Latin bilis), also known as gall, is a yellow-green fluid produced by the liver of most vertebrates that aids the digestion of lipids in the small intestine.
One of the largest, longest-lived trees in the Amazon, this species produces a fruit and shell weighing up to two kilograms, with edible seeds famed for their selenium content — what tree is it?
Brazil nut (Bertholletia excelsa) refers to a South American tree of the monotypic genus Bertholletia in the family Lecythidaceae as well as the tree's commercially-harvested edible seeds.
Wolves, domestic dogs, coyotes, and golden jackals all belong to this taxonomic genus, whose members are known for massive skulls, long legs, and short ears and tails. Name the genus?
Canis is a genus of the Caninae which includes multiple extant species, such as wolves, dogs, coyotes, and golden jackals.

A member of the poppy family found across Europe and western Asia, this herbaceous plant is nicknamed 'greater celandine' and isn't actually related to the similarly-named 'lesser celandine' — what's its scientific name?
Chelidonium majus is a perennial herbaceous flowering plant in the poppy family Papaveraceae.
Once a standard topical anesthetic prized for narrowing blood vessels, this tropane alkaloid is extracted from the leaves of South American coca plants — which substance is it?
Cocaine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant and tropane alkaloid, derived primarily from the leaves of two coca species native to South America.
This blood-feeding parasitic insect usually lives in human pubic hair and is thought to have diverged from a closely related gorilla parasite roughly 3.3 million years ago — what is it?
Crab louse (Pthirus pubis) is an insect that is an obligate ectoparasite of humans, feeding exclusively on blood.
A colorless, volatile liquid (CH2Cl2) with a sweet, chloroform-like odor, it's slightly polar, mixes with many organic solvents but not water, and is widely used as a solvent — what is it?
Dichloromethane (DCM, methylene chloride, or methylene bichloride) is an organochlorine compound with the formula CH2Cl2.
Born in German Pomerania and drawn by Franz Boas into documenting Native American languages, this anthropologist became a founding giant of American linguistics — who was he?

Edward Sapir (January 26, 1884 - February 4, 1939) was an American anthropologist-linguist, and one of the most important figures in the development of the discipline of linguistics in the United States.
This recurring set of hormone-driven reproductive changes in female mammals is interrupted by 'rest' phases and pregnancy, and has a male equivalent called rut — what is it?

Estrous cycle (from Latin oestrus 'frenzy', originally from Ancient Greek (ostros) 'gadfly') is a set of recurring physiological changes induced by reproductive hormones in females of mammalian subclass Theria.
Found on sperm cells, fungal spores and countless microbes, this tail-like structure provides motility and even senses moisture in some swarming bacteria — what is it?

Flagellum (pl.: flagella) (Latin for 'whip' or 'scourge') is a hair-like appendage that protrudes from certain plant and animal sperm cells, from fungal spores (zoospores), and from a wide range of microorganisms to provide motility.

A Belgian-British emigrant to New York, this inventor struck gold during a 1906 stay in Central America by perfecting an early instant-coffee process and building a company to mass-produce it — who was he?
George Washington (inventor) (May 20, 1871 - March 29, 1946) was a Belgian-British inventor and businessman.

Caused by a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens, this non-cancerous condition results in enlarged breast tissue in men and can occur in newborns, adolescents, and older or obese men — name the condition?

Gynecomastia (also spelled gynaecomastia) is the non-cancerous enlargement of one or both breasts in men due to the growth of breast tissue as a result of a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens.
With species ranging from evergreen trees to climbing shrubs across the tropics and temperate zones, this genus's most iconic species decorates Christmas cards worldwide — what genus is it?
Holly is a genus of over 570 species of flowering plants in the family Aquifoliaceae, and the only living genus in that family.
More than 20 types make up this genetic skin condition, whose Greek-derived name means "fish" — a nod to its hallmark dry, thickened, scaly texture — which disorder?
Ichthyosis is a family of genetic skin disorders characterized by dry, thickened, scaly skin.
This NASA astronaut and Marine Corps test pilot commanded the SpaceX Crew-7 mission and served as a flight engineer aboard the International Space Station — who is she?
Jasmin Moghbeli (born June 24, 1983) is an American U.S.

This American game show host and former software engineer won 74 consecutive games on a legendary quiz show in 2004, the longest streak in its history, before becoming its host himself in 2021 — who is he?
Ken Jennings (born May 23, 1974) is an American game show host and author who has hosted the syndicated quiz show Jeopardy!
Distinguished from its cousins the pikas by short furry tails and elongated ears and hind legs, this mammal family comprises over 70 species we commonly call rabbits and hares — which family?
Leporidae is the family of rabbits and hares (Lepus), containing over 70 species of extant mammals in all.
This German physicist gave aerodynamics its rigorous mathematical footing, identifying the boundary layer and lifting-line theory — and a dimensionless number bears his name. Who was he?
Ludwig Prandtl (German; 4 February 1875 - 15 August 1953) was a German fluid dynamicist, physicist and aerospace scientist.
Often called the 'father of the handheld cell phone,' this Motorola engineer placed the first public mobile call in 1973 from a New York City sidewalk — who is he?
Martin Cooper (inventor) (born December 26, 1928) is an American engineer.
Built primarily from stainless steel, this Soviet supersonic interceptor could exceed Mach 3.2, but doing so risked wrecking its own engines. What aircraft is it?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-25 (NATO reporting name: Foxbat) is a supersonic interceptor and reconnaissance aircraft that is among the fastest military aircraft to enter service.

This symbiotic relationship between a fungus and a plant, in which fungal threads interconnect with plant roots at the cellular level, plays a major role in plant nutrition and soil chemistry — what is it called?

Born in New York to Jewish Holocaust-survivor parents, this Princeton-trained political scientist studies the politics of the Holocaust and the Israeli–Palestinian conflict — and his 2007 DePaul tenure fight made headlines. Who is he?
Norman Finkelstein (born December 8, 1953) is an American political scientist and activist.
Triggered by a surge of luteinizing hormone near the midpoint of the cycle, this event sees an ovarian follicle rupture and release an egg ready to be fertilized. What's the term?
Ovulation is an important part of the menstrual cycle in female vertebrates where the egg cells are released from the ovaries as part of the ovarian cycle.
What medical term describes damage or disease affecting the nerves — impairing sensation, movement, gland, or organ function — commonly caused by systemic diseases such as diabetes?

Peripheral neuropathy is damage or disease affecting the nerves. Peripheral neuropathy may be acute (with sudden onset, rapid progress) or chronic (symptoms begin subtly and progress slowly), and may be reversible or permanent.
A member of the cashew family and a priority tree-nut allergen, this green seed saw the US, Iran, and Turkey produce 87% of the world's 1.4 million tonnes in 2024 — what is it?
Pistachio (UK also; Pistacia vera) is a small to medium-sized tree of the cashew family.

This endogenous steroid sex hormone plays a central role in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryonic development, and also serves as a key metabolic intermediate for producing other steroid hormones — name the hormone?
Progesterone (P4) is an endogenous steroid and progestogen sex hormone involved in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryogenesis of humans and other species.
Bitter-tasting and rich in vitamin K, this Mediterranean vegetable with edible buds resembling broccoli is also known as broccoli rabe — what is it?
Rapini (broccoli rabe or raab; RAHB) is a green cruciferous vegetable, with the leaves, buds, and stems all being edible; the buds somewhat resemble broccoli.
Discovered in 1973 by Ruth Bishop via electron micrographs, this virus is the leading cause of diarrheal disease in infants worldwide, spread via the fecal-oral route — what is it?
Rotavirus are the most common cause of diarrhoeal disease among infants and young children.
Which chemical element, symbol Se, was discovered in 1817 by Jöns Jacob Berzelius and named for the moon, in a nod to its chemical similarity to tellurium, named for the Earth?
Selenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Se and atomic number 34.
This alkaline compound, commonly diluted in water and sold as household bleach, is derived from hypochlorous acid and is unstable in its pure anhydrous form. What is it?
Sodium hypochlorite is an alkaline inorganic chemical compound with the formula NaOCl (also written as NaClO).
A Jamaican-British Marxist sociologist who co-founded New Left Review, this thinker became a founding figure of the Birmingham School of Cultural Studies — who was he?
Stuart Hall (cultural theorist) (3 February 1932 - 10 February 2014) was a Jamaican-British Marxist sociologist, cultural theorist, and political activist.

This family of marine and freshwater fish can inflate themselves dramatically, revealing thin spines that stay hidden against their skin until they puff up — unlike their spinier, porcupine-like relatives — name this fish family?
Tetraodontidae is a family of marine and freshwater fish in the order Tetraodontiformes.
Usually caused by mutations in the TCOF1 gene, which autosomal dominant condition affects facial bone and ear development but not intelligence?
Treacher Collins syndrome (TCS) is a genetic disorder characterized by deformities of the ears, eyes, cheekbones, and chin.
Regarded as the 'Father of the Indian space program,' this physicist and astronomer also helped develop nuclear power in India, earning the Padma Vibhushan posthumously — who is he?
Vikram Sarabhai (12 August 1919 - 30 December 1971) was an Indian physicist and astronomer who initiated space research and helped to develop nuclear power in India.

This unit of time is based on how long Earth takes to complete one full orbit around the Sun, with the precise scientific definition running about 365 days, 5 hours, and 48 minutes — what unit is this?

Year is a unit of time based on how long it takes the Earth to orbit the Sun. In scientific use, the tropical year (approximately 365 solar days, 5 hours, 48 minutes, 45 seconds) and the sidereal year (about 20 minutes longer) are more exact.
Also called sweet flag, this wetland plant contains psychoactive compounds and has been banned from American food products despite centuries of use in traditional medicine — which species?
Acorus calamus: Species of plant. Acorus calamus (also called sweet flag, sway or muskrat root, among many other common names) is a species of flowering plant with psychoactive chemicals.
This congenital condition causes a total or partial absence of pigment, leading to white hair, pale skin, and often pink or reddish eyes — what is it called?
Albinism: Disorder causing lack of pigmentation.
Despite being named after a European bird for its reddish-orange breast, this thrush is the most abundant landbird on its continent, numbering some 370 million individuals — what is it?
American robin: Species of bird. The American robin (Turdus migratorius) is a migratory bird of the true thrush genus and Turdidae, the wider thrush family.
Native to Africa, India, the Middle East and Central Asia, these fleet-footed members of the family Bovidae aren't actually one single evolutionary group — what are they?
Ranging from a racing tachycardia to a sluggish bradycardia, this catch-all term covers any heartbeat that strays from normal sinus rhythm — what is it called?
Arrhythmia: Group of medical conditions characterized by irregular heartbeat.
Derived from a Greek word meaning 'that which is thought worthy,' which term denotes a statement accepted as true without proof, serving as a starting point for further reasoning?
Axiom: Statement that is taken to be true.
This common, noncancerous enlargement of a male gland can cause frequent urination and a weak stream; it isn't linked to poor hygiene, and there's no known cure. What's the condition?
Benign prostatic hyperplasia: Noncancerous increase in size of the prostate gland.
Your blood type is set by antigens sitting on the surface of which cells?
Inherited proteins, carbohydrates and glycolipids on the red cell surface define the group. Some of the same antigens appear on other tissues too.
Grown on one of the Amazon's largest and longest-lived trees, this selenium-rich edible seed comes in a shell weighing up to 2 kilograms combined with its fruit. What is it?
Brazil nut: Species of tree and its edible seeds.
Native to tropical Africa, this gourd-producing vine yields fruit that can be eaten young as a vegetable or dried and hollowed out into bowls, ladles, or even musical instruments — what is it?
Calabash: Species of bottle gourd plant.

Born in London, raised in Milan, and self-taught in web design, this Catholic teenager built a website cataloguing Eucharistic miracles before dying of leukemia at fifteen — he was beatified in 2020. Who was he?

With about 3,400 species in over 520 genera, this insect family includes nearly every member of its group except two species in a small sister taxon — which family?
This umbrella term covers mental processes like perception, attention, memory, and reasoning that let us acquire and apply knowledge — what is it called?
Cognition: Mental process dealing with knowledge.
This mostly inactive steroid hormone is created when an enzyme shields organs like the kidneys by converting active cortisol into its inactive form — what is it?
Cortisone: Corticosteroid precursor and metabolite of cortisol.
Started in 1955 by an army colonel and a cynologist as an experiment, this hybrid dog breed became officially recognized as a national breed in 1982 — which one?
Czechoslovakian Wolfdog: Czech and Slovak breed of dog.
Native to the Mediterranean and nicknamed 'clove pink' for a spicy fragrance reminiscent of cinnamon and nutmeg, what flower is this?
Dianthus caryophyllus: Species of flowering plant.
This Eastern Han hydrologist is credited as the first to harness a waterwheel to power the bellows of a blast furnace for forging cast iron — who was this ingenious engineer?
Du Shi: 1st-century engineer, metallurgist and politician.
This Hungarian nuclear chemist became the world's leading expert in isotope separation and polonium preparation, and confirmed the existence of "Uranium-Y" — who was she?
This class of chemical compound forms when an acid's hydroxyl hydrogen is swapped for an organic group, and includes the glycerides that make up most animal fats — what is it?
Ester: Compound derived from an acid.

Recognized by their pod-like fruit and compound leaves, this plant family — the third-largest among flowering plants — includes beans, peas, and lentils along with genera like Acacia and Mimosa. What family is it?
Fabaceae: Family of legume flowering plants. Fabaceae or Leguminosae, commonly known as the legume, pea, or bean family, is a large and agriculturally important family of flowering plants.
Belonging to a bird family that's the only survivor of its order, this wading bird comes in four American species plus two more across Africa and Eurasia — what is it?
Flamingo: Family of birds. There are four flamingo species distributed throughout the Americas (including the Caribbean), and two species native to Afro-Eurasia.
Marketed as Neurontin, this anticonvulsant and GABA derivative is prescribed for nerve pain and partial seizures by binding to the α2δ subunits of calcium channels — what is it?

Caused by excess growth hormone before a child's growth plates fuse — usually from a pituitary tumor — this rare disorder produces height at least three standard deviations above average. What condition is it?
Gigantism: Human growth disorder. It is a rare disorder resulting from increased levels of growth hormone before the fusion of the growth plate which usually occurs at some point soon after puberty.
The largest and most widespread member of its rosy-pink family, this wading bird ranges from Sub-Saharan Africa to the Mediterranean and Central Asia — which species?
Caused by mutations in the ABCA12 gene, this severe genetic skin disorder covers newborns in thick, cracked plates resembling armor — what is it?
Harlequin-type ichthyosis: Genetic skin disease. Harlequin-type ichthyosis is a genetic disorder that results in thickened skin over nearly the entire body at birth.

This American philosopher co-created an algorithm for the Boolean satisfiability problem and helped prove Hilbert's tenth problem unsolvable — all while reshaping the philosophy of mind and language. Who was he?
Hilary Putnam: American mathematician and philosopher (1926–2016)
Marketed under the brand name Plaquenil, this oral medication treats malaria as well as rheumatoid arthritis and lupus, though it can cause retinopathy with long-term use — what drug is it?
Hydroxychloroquine: Antimalarial medication. It is taken by mouth, often in the form of hydroxychloroquine sulfate.

According to psychologist Alfred Adler, this persistent feeling of being deficient or lesser than others — often stemming from childhood comparisons to a sibling — can lead people to overcompensate. What is it called?
Inferiority complex: Intense feeling of inadequacy and inferior.

His 1962 book The Calculus of Consent launched a theory of how politicians' and bureaucrats' self-interest shapes their decisions, earning him the 1986 Nobel in economics — which founder of public choice theory is this?
James M. Buchanan: American economist and Nobel Laureate (1919–2013)
Dubbed the 'Angel of Death,' this German physician held doctorates in both anthropology and medicine before joining the SS and selecting Auschwitz prisoners for the gas chambers — who was he?
Josef Mengele: Nazi SS doctor at Auschwitz (1911–1979)
Also called German turnip despite not being related to true turnips, this stout cabbage cultivar can be eaten raw or cooked, stem and leaves alike — what vegetable?
Kohlrabi: Biennial cultivar of wild cabbage.
Also known as Peruvian ginseng, this Andean root crop is grown at high altitude in Peru and Bolivia and exported worldwide as a dietary powder — what plant is it?
Lepidium meyenii: Plant species native to South America.
Based on the L-188 Electra airliner and distinguished by a tail 'stinger' used to magnetically detect submarines, this four-engine turboprop has served the US Navy since the 1960s — which aircraft?
Lockheed P-3 Orion: Maritime patrol and anti-submarine aircraft family.
Occurring naturally as the mineral brucite, this poorly soluble white solid neutralizes stomach acid in a well-known antacid — which compound?

A hemiparasitic plant that taps into its host tree via a structure called the haustorium to steal water and nutrients, its European species was introduced to Northern California in 1900 — what plant is it?
Mistletoe: Common name for various parasitic plants.

Grouping over 30 inherited disorders that cause progressive weakening and wasting of skeletal tissue — with the Duchenne form affecting roughly half of all cases in young boys — what's this disease group called?
Muscular dystrophy: Diseases in which skeletal and visceral muscles break down over time.
Named after a German physical chemist, this electrochemistry formula calculates a reaction's reduction potential from temperature, electron count, and reactant concentrations — which relationship?
Nernst equation: Physical law in electrochemistry.
Practitioners of this field are sometimes mistaken for mere coin collectors, but they study all means of paying debts — even the horses the Kyrgyz once used as currency. What's the field called?
Numismatics: Study of currencies, coins and paper money.
Named from Greek words meaning 'porous bones,' this disorder causes bone density loss serious enough that fractures can occur with minor stress, especially in the elderly — what is it?
Osteoporosis: Skeletal disorder. Osteoporosis is the most common reason for a broken bone among the elderly.
Also known as trisomy 13, this chromosomal condition arises when cells carry extra genetic material from chromosome 13, causing widespread organ defects — which syndrome?
Patau syndrome: Chromosomal disorder in which there are three copies of chromosome 13.

Derived in 1900 by a German physicist who proposed that an oscillator's energy could only change in discrete increments, this principle describes the spectral density of radiation from a black body at a given temperature — what is it called?
Planck's law: Spectral density of light emitted by a black body.
This common name describes small aquatic crustaceans with an exoskeleton and ten legs, especially popular in the UK and Commonwealth nations for larger swimming decapods — what is it?
Prawn: Common name applied to some types of crustaceans.
Ranging from Penguin Random House to countless small independent players, which broad industry covers making books, magazines, music, and software available to the public, in print or digital form?

In a late stage of stellar evolution, this puffed-up, low-to-intermediate-mass star has a surface temperature around 5,000 K and burns helium or hydrogen in shells around its core — what type of star is it?
Red giant: Type of large cool star.
Also called a dassie, this small African and Middle Eastern mammal lives in crevice colonies of up to 80 and posts lookouts to warn of approaching predators — which animal?

Springbok: Antelope of southwest and south Africa. The springbok or springbuck (Antidorcas marsupialis) is an antelope found mainly in south and southwest Africa.

Sulfur: Chemical element with atomic number 16 (S)
From Greek for 'arrangement' and 'method', this science names and classifies organisms into ranked groups — domain, kingdom, phylum, and on down to species — what is the field?

When a piece of one of these blood-vessel clots breaks free to travel the body it's called an embolus — and the original blockage can trigger a stroke or heart attack. What is this clot formation called?
Thrombosis: Formation of blood clots inside the blood vessels.
Also known as all-trans retinoic acid, this medication treats acne as a topical cream but must be taken orally for leukemia patients with a specific gene fusion — what is it?
Tretinoin: Medication. Tretinoin, also known as all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA), is a medication used for the treatment of acne and acute promyelocytic leukemia.
Known as the Great Bear, this constellation contains the seven-star pattern nicknamed the Big Dipper — what's it called?
Ursa Major: Constellation in the northern sky.
Sporting prominent tusks and whiskers, this Arctic pinniped's Pacific males can weigh over 2,000 kilograms, making it second in size among pinnipeds only to the elephant seals — what animal?
Walrus: Species of marine mammal with tusks.
Named for the Aztec god of fire and lightning, this ancient Mexican dog breed comes in hairless and fully-coated varieties within the same litter — which breed?
Xoloitzcuintle: Hairless dog breed from Mexico.
